review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked each new definition against Mathlib: ofFiniteCard, ofFiniteIndex, profiniteOrder, profiniteIndex, trivialClosedSubgroup, wholeClosedSubgroup, wholeOpenNormalSubgroup, FiniteAddSubgroup and torsionOrder.

- Supernatural numbers: a grep of Mathlib finds no supernatural-number concept, so the order and index definitions have nothing to duplicate.
- Closed subgroups: Mathlib's ClosedSubgroup (Topology/Algebra/Group/ClosedSubgroup.lean) has only SetLike, PartialOrder and Min/SemilatticeInf instances. It has no Top or Bot, so trivialClosedSubgroup and wholeClosedSubgroup fill a gap rather than compete.
- Open normal subgroups: OpenSubgroup has a Top instance, but OpenNormalSubgroup does not, so wholeOpenNormalSubgroup is not a duplicate either.
- FiniteAddSubgroup: I found no Mathlib bundled type of finite subgroups. It is a plain subtype of AddSubgroup A, used only here and not parallel to any Mathlib concept.

Lean core and Batteries were not searched exhaustively. No competing concept turned up, so I abstained.
